brief: A portable electronics organizer: a base with removable bins for small parts, at least one drawer, and a carry handle.

requirements.evidence: piece:0,0,0;full plus piece:0,-1,0;half-s, joined with jointBolt:0#0,-1#5 and with open faces capped

bin:0,0,0~hex-bin-half-div3 is a drop-in tray with 3 compartments. It hangs on its own rim, so it lifts out. It is staged with M3 screws, nuts and standoffs. These sit under the top cover, so they can't be seen from outside.
drawer:0#0,-1#cut on the half base. Props could not be staged inside the closed drawer (PROP_NO_REST).
handle:0,0,0;top on cover:0,0,0;full;top with its inserts. Only the shape is checked: the configurator does not rate how much load the handle can carry.
Small 2-cell footprint with a top handle, and the bin is closed in under the lid. Strength and how well things stay put while carried are not checked.

finish.summary: Compact two-cell organizer: a full hex base holding a removable half-depth 3-compartment bin, with a top cover and a carry handle; a south half base joined to it carries a drawer on its cut face. Open faces are capped, joints are bolted, and check_build is clean with meshClash clear.

M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
